title: Defense Budget and Acquisition: Research & Analysis | CSIS
text:
Defense Budget and Acquisition

CSIS experts track the foremost budget issues in the defense policy sphere, exploring trends in the overall defense budget, military readiness, force structure, defense acquisition, and military compensation in a broader effort to assess the alignment of the country’s defense strategy and its resources.

Image

Photo: Andriy Onufriyenko/Getty Images

Understanding the U.S. Federal Government’s AI Spending

Federal agencies obligated $4.1 billion across 2,255 AI-related contracts since FY 2019, and 83 percent of those dollars went to the Defense Department. The CSIS Futures Lab follows the money trail and tracks the evolution of federal AI demand.

Winning the Salvo Competition: How to Rebuild the Air and Missile Defense Industrial Base

Recent wars show that the side able to replenish interceptors fastest will shape the military balance. The United States and Europe should turn surge spending into durable capacity through predictable demand, shared investment, and coordinated production.

How Quickly Can the DOD Rebuild and Recast the Munitions Industrial Base?

The U.S. munitions industrial base must be rebuilt and recast for modern wars of precision and attrition. By analyzing DOD budget documents and industry announcements, Dr. Jerry McGinn clarifies the planned future and remaining challenges to achieving this goal.
